steps.body: One residual judges one point. All the residuals together judge the MODEL. Plot each residual against x — flip the line down to a flat zero-axis — and look for a pattern. A good fit leaves patternless scatter; a pattern means the line missed something systematic.
Diagnose a suspicious set of leftovers.

widget.prompt: A line was fit to data. Reading left to right, the residuals run: +3, +1, −1, −2, −1, +1, +3 — positive, dipping negative, positive again. Verdict?

options.label: The relationship curves — a line was the wrong tool
The fit is fine — some residuals are always nonzero
options.feedback: Nonzero is expected; ORGANIZED is the problem. Ends up, middle down is a U — a curve's signature.

options.label: One outlier is dragging the line
options.feedback: An outlier makes ONE big residual. Here every residual follows the same sweep — that's structure, not one bad point.

widget.successFeedback: A U in the leftovers means the data bends: the line overshoots the middle and undershoots the ends. The residual plot is the model's X-ray.

steps.body: Force the best straight line through curved data — then read its leftovers.

widget.prompt: The data is y = x² in disguise: (1,1), (2,4), (3,9), (4,16). Fit the best straight line you can.
widget.successFeedback: Best straight effort: ŷ = 5x − 5. Its leftovers read +1, −1, −1, +1 — ends above, middle below. No slope or shift removes that arc; the pattern is the data announcing it is not straight.
widget.slopeFeedback: Watch the ENDS against the middle: curved data will always leave the outer points on one side of a straight line and the inner points on the other.
widget.offsetFeedback: The tilt is close — now slide b until the misses straddle the line instead of piling on one side.

predict.prompt: If the true relationship is curved and you force a straight line through it, the leftovers will…

options.label: Form a pattern — misses organized by x
Still scatter randomly — errors are errors

predict.reveal: The line can't bend, so it must miss systematically: under at the ends, over in the middle (or vice versa). The residual plot turns that hidden bias into a visible U. Random scatter is what a CORRECT model leaves behind.

steps.body: Count the pattern you just built.
explanationVariants: The straight line overshoots curved data in the middle and undershoots at the ends, so exactly the two middle residuals are negative.
Compute all four against ŷ = 5x − 5: +1, −1, −1, +1. Two negatives — the middle pair, the curvature signature.

widget.prompt: With the best line ŷ = 5x − 5 in place, how many of the four residuals are NEGATIVE?

commonErrors.feedback: A best fit does not erase misses — the middle points (2,4) and (3,9) sit BELOW this line: 4 < 5 and 9 < 10.
The END points sit ABOVE the line: 1 > 0 and 16 > 15 — their residuals are positive. Only the middle pair goes negative.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Residuals under ŷ = 5x − 5: 1−0 = +1, 4−5 = −1, 9−10 = −1, 16−15 = +1. Two are negative.
widget.successFeedback: Two — the middle pair. Plus, minus, minus, plus: the arc a straight line cannot flatten.

explanationVariants: Patternless residuals — signs mixed, sizes similar across x — mean the line captured all the structure there was.
A good model's leftovers look like noise, because noise is all that's left.

widget.prompt: Which residual picture says 'the line fits well'?

options.label: Signs mixed, no trend, similar sizes everywhere
options.feedback: Structureless leftovers: the line took all the signal, leaving only noise.

options.label: A clean U shape
options.feedback: A U means unmodeled curvature — the line failed.

options.label: Small on the left, huge on the right
options.feedback: Growing misses mean the relationship's spread changes with x — one line can't be equally trusted everywhere.

widget.successFeedback: Fit well ⇒ leftovers are boring. Interesting residuals are bad news for the model.

explanationVariants: Residuals all positive means every observation beat the prediction — the line sits uniformly too low.
A line placed correctly must have leftovers on both sides; one-sided misses are a placement error, not noise.

widget.prompt: Every residual comes out positive. The fitted line is…

options.label: Too low — the whole cloud floats above it
options.feedback: Observed beats predicted everywhere: raise the line.

options.label: Too high
options.feedback: All-positive means observed > predicted — the line is UNDER the data.

options.label: Perfect — positivity is good
options.feedback: Good fits balance their misses; all-positive is systematic under-prediction.

widget.successFeedback: Residuals should straddle zero. One-sided leftovers mean the line needs to move, not that the world is generous.

steps.body: Three diagnoses so far: U = curvature, one-sided = misplaced line, growing spread = the relationship loosens with x. Different diseases, one instrument — and none of them are visible from the fitted line alone. The scatter plot can look fine while the residual plot screams.

hints: Compute each residual under ŷ = x + 1: data (1, 2), (2, 4), (3, 4), (4, 5).
Three zeros and one +1 — is that a pattern organized by x, or one loose point?
explanationVariants: Residuals 0, +1, 0, 0: no sweep, no side, no growth — just one modest miss at x = 2. The line stands.
A pattern needs organization across x; a single nonzero residual among zeros is ordinary noise.

widget.prompt: Data: (1,2), (2,4), (3,4), (4,5). Line: ŷ = x + 1. What do the residuals say?

options.label: 0, +1, 0, 0 — no pattern; the line fits
options.feedback: Three exact hits, one small miss, no organization: healthy.

options.label: They form a U — curvature
options.feedback: U needs ends-up-middle-down (or the reverse). 0, +1, 0, 0 has no sweep.

options.label: All positive — the line is too low
options.feedback: Three residuals are exactly zero; only one is positive. That's a point, not a placement.

widget.successFeedback: You just ran the diagnostic numerically. The instrument works without a single picture.

steps.body: Why bother, if the scatter looked fine?
explanationVariants: The fitted line visually dominates a scatter plot, hiding small systematic misses; zeroing it out makes the misses the whole picture.
Residual plots amplify what the eye discounts: structure a hundred times smaller than the trend still shows as a clear pattern.

widget.prompt: Why plot residuals instead of just eyeballing the line through the scatter?

options.label: Reveal small, systematic departures
options.feedback: The steep line dwarfs 1-unit misses; against a flat zero line the same misses are unmissable.

options.label: Make the graph quicker to draw
options.feedback: Simplicity isn't the point — sensitivity is.

options.label: Satisfy a standard plotting rule
options.feedback: The convention exists because it catches what eyeballing misses.

widget.successFeedback: Flattening the trend is signal processing: subtract what you know to expose what you don't.

steps.body: Leftovers, read together, audit the model.
takeaways: A well-fit line leaves patternless residuals — boring leftovers are good news.
U-shape ⇒ curvature; one-sided ⇒ misplaced line; growing spread ⇒ trust varies with x.
The residual plot magnifies structure the raw scatter hides.
steps.teaser: Last step: use the leftovers as a steering wheel — adjust the line until they balance.
